in healthy women with induced potassium depletion: 1) the increased generation of angiotensin-II and the decreased synthesis of vasodilating prostaglandins contribute to the expression of hypokalemia-induced renal dysfunction; 2) the increased generation and decreased synthesis of medullary prostaglandins, in the face to the increased generation of vasopressor angiotensin and the reduced synthesis of cortical vasodilators, antagonize the effects of vasopressant
the increased generation of angiotensin and the decreased synthesis of prostanoids contribute to renal hypokalemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effective role of the prostanoids and AT II in the expression of renal function in hypokalemia.
the effective role played by the AT II and prostanoids on the renal hypokalemia.
the role of prostanoids in the regulation of the renal function and the relationship with the angiotensinogen-AT I-AT II system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the renal hypokalemia-induced changes in the synthesis and release of vasopressor and vasodilator factors contribute to the expression of the functional renal hypokalemia-induced changes in the renal hemodynamics and tubular function, and that the renal hypocalcemia-induced changes in the prostanoids and AT II synthesis and release are probably the most effective components of the renal functional adaptation to hypokalemia.
the prostanoids, AT II, and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system play a role in the renal response to potassium depletion.
the prostanoid system, as well as AT II, exerted an important and effective role in the renal hypokalemia-induced dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the renal hypokalemia-induced dysfunction is not a simple consequence of the decreased renal potassium secretion but it is a complex phenomenon which involves a series of interrelated mechanisms, among which the decreased synthesis of prostanoids in the renal cortex and the increased production of angiotensin in the kidney are the most important ones.
the prostanoids and the renin-angiotensin system exerted opposite effects in the renal hypokalemia.

the renal hypokalemia-induced dysfunction, as a result of the decreased synthesis of prostanoid mediators and the increased generation of angiotensin, represents an adaptive mechanism to the potassium depletion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in potassium depletion, the increased production of renal AT II, in the face to the decreased synthesis of prostanoids, contributed to the renal hypokalemia and the increased urinary excretion of chloride and potassium.

in potassium depletion the increased generation of angiotensin and the decreased production of cortical vasodilator prostanoids and medullary vasodilator and antivasopressin prostanoids are responsible for the expression of renal dysfunction.
the renal hypokalemia is a complex phenomenon that involves the interplay between several vasoactive systems.
